message.content:
Lapel pins of 10K gold with stones are most likely classified as jewelry of precious metal, heading 7113. Subheading 7113.19 covers articles of jewelry of other precious metal, whether or not plated or clad with precious metal. Lapel pins are not necklaces, bracelets, or other named articles, so they fall under "other articles of jewelry" (7113.19.50). The statistical suffix is 7113.19.5000 for other jewelry of precious metal (gold), valued over $18 per dozen pieces... Actually the HTSUS structure is 7113.19.10 (rope, curb, etc. chain), 7113.19.21 (articles for personal adornment not otherwise specified, e.g. necklaces), 7113.19.25 (clasps, etc.), 7113.19.29 (other, gold, other than rope/chain), 7113.19.50 (other: of precious metal). Lapel pins would fall in 7113.19.50, with the 10-digit being 7113.19.5000 (the actual line is 7113.19.50 with statistical suffixes 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70...).

Rulings on similar service-award lapel pins in gold with stones commonly use 7113.19.5000. I'll go with 7113.19.5000. Counter-consideration: heading 7113 requires jewelry, which includes small objects of personal adornment, and lapel pins qualify. Gold 10K is precious metal (at least 10K is permitted for gold).
